html:
Fedon's rebellion was a rising in Grenada in 1795 and 1796 led by Julien Fedon, a free planter of mixed race, against British rule. It drew in many free people of colour, French settlers and enslaved Africans.

Inspired by the French Revolution and backed by the French agent Victor Hugues, the rebels held most of the island for over a year. They killed the British governor and dozens of other prisoners.

British troops crushed the rising in 1796. Fedon was never found. The rebellion came at the same time as the Second Carib War on St Vincent and the Haitian Revolution, part of a wave that shook the Caribbean slave colonies.
